text:
anya: quick sync — thinking about a refactor to heap consolidation. idea: move compaction into a background per-tenant worker + admission quotas so one noisy tenant can't thrash the whole host. thoughts?

rui: sounds promising. main risk i see is compaction thrash during request bursts — we need an admission gate tied to live IO/latency signals.

sam: agree. we should throttle compaction based on eviction rate + IO pressure. heuristic: if compact_io_bytes/s > 100MB or host_p99_latency > 200ms then back off for that tenant.

elena: ownership question — current approach uses a global compaction lock which blocks allocations during handover. can we switch to token-based ownership per arena to avoid global stalls? sketch: `compaction_token = allocate_token(tenant_id)` then execute only if token valid.

frank: also watch KV/cache interactions — aggressive compaction can kick hot KV entries out of cache and spike latency. we need a rule to protect hot regions (prefetch/hint).

anya: sketching a proposal: 3-stage flow: MARK -> PLAN -> EXECUTE.
- MARK: quick pass to identify candidate segments and attach metadata (no heavy IO).
- PLAN: compute region list under a lightweight snapshot (no global lock), estimate reclaimable bytes and IO cost.
- EXECUTE: acquire tenant token and perform IO-limited compaction with throttling.
This keeps the expensive work gated and makes abort cheap.

infra-bot: perfbench queued: job #4621 for heap-compact microbench (will post results).

rui: for the PLAN step we can simulate cost with a cheap sampler instead of full scan. add config knobs: `plan_sample_ratio` and `max_plan_time_ms`.

sam: telemetry we need: per-tenant compact_ops/sec, reclaim_bytes, compact_io_bytes, compact_pause_seconds, compact_abort_reasons. alert if `compaction_paused > 30s` for core tenants.

elena: operational question: should compaction be best-effort on Dedicated but enforced on Hosted (since Hosted needs stronger fragmentation guarantees)? that affects how strict token grants are.

frank: suggest canary rollout on a small Dedicated fleet first, then Hosted low-traffic zone. :shipit:

anya: i'll draft an RFC with the 3-stage flow, token semantics, config knobs and the telemetry set. will include perf targets and a simple cost model (io bytes -> estimated latency impact). tagging @elena @sam to review when ready.

elena: +1. please include abort metrics and expected SLO deltas for tenants.

sam: +1 from me — add a small fuzz test that simulates bursty requests during plan/exec to validate no regressions.

anya: thanks all — i'll post the RFC link here when it's up.
